Genuine, verified nuance in the source's OWN comment: staggerSelectedLayers (motion.js:12685-12698, past this span, sibling-covered) is prefaced by the comment 'so both routes to the same result agree'. Traced precisely: staggerSelectedLayers sorts `_layerSel` ASCENDING BY ARRAY INDEX (`function(a,b){return a-b;}`) and anchors rank 0 (smallest index); this span's own buildLayerRows/startLayerSkewDrag instead sort by ACTUAL ON-SCREEN visual top position (`getBoundingClientRect().top`), explicitly because 'the layer list renders newest-on-top, so index order is visually REVERSED' (this span's own comment, 12189). Since ascending-index order is thus the exact reverse permutation of ascending-visual-top order for a flat selection (confirmed against computeLayerRenderOrder, timeline.js:5600-5603, which iterates `for(var i=state.layers.length-1;i>=0;i--)`, i.e. highest index first = topmost on screen), staggerSelectedLayers's rank-0 anchor (smallest index) is the BOTTOM-most row on screen, and its displacement `step*rank` grows toward the TOP-most row — which matches this span's own onLayerSkewMove exactly for `mode==='top'` (anchor at the bottom-most visual row, `f=1` i.e. full displacement at the top-most row) but is the OPPOSITE of `mode==='bottom'` (which anchors the TOP-most row and moves the bottom-most row fully). The comment's claim of agreement is therefore correct for one of the two skew-drag directions and not literally true for the other; more importantly, the two routes differ in SCOPE regardless of direction — staggerSelectedLayers rewrites only `track.keys[].frame` values (property keyframes) and never touches `ld.inPoint`/`ld.outPoint` or calls SM.shiftLayerFrames, while this span's own onLayerSkewUp/retimeLayers path (packet 2) shifts `ld.inPoint`/`ld.outPoint` live during the drag AND, once at drop, both the layer's stored frame CONTENT (SM.shiftLayerFrames) and its property keys (SMMotion.shiftLayerMotionKeys) together. This is a documentation precision recorded against the source's own comment, not a correction to any validated range in either artifact.

packets.responsibility: Section header (12175) plus its own 8-line feedback-driven design comment (12176-12182: whole-LAYER selection staggers EVERY animated property's EVERY key for that layer together, matching a reference GIF, no need to expand a Transform group or marquee individual diamonds). `_layerStaggerBoxEl` (12183) is the sole DOM handle for the layer box, `null` when absent. removeLayerStaggerBox (12184-12186): removes and nulls it, idempotent. buildLayerRows (12195-12213), preceded by an 8-line comment (12187-12194) explaining its own visual-order sort and why empty-of-keys layers still occupy a row (interpolation-fraction spacing): sorts `_layerSel.slice()` by each layer's own `#frame-grid .frow[data-layer]` `getBoundingClientRect().top` (falls back to `a-b`, i.e. array-index order, if either DOM row is missing), then for each ordered layer index builds one `entries` array covering EVERY `propsFor(h)` property that has a `trackFor(h,prop)` track, pushing `{track,key,orig:k.frame}` for every one of that track's keys — `rows` is thus one entry per selected layer (in on-screen top-to-bottom order), each itself a flat list of every animated key across every property of that one layer (layers with zero animated keys still get an empty array, preserving row count/order for the interpolation math in packet 2/3). noKeysGuard (12223-12227), preceded by a 6-line comment (12214-12222) explaining the deliberate reuse of layer-inout's own group-bar drag rather than a second implementation for move ('Skew and Space genuinely need keys — there is no bar equivalent... They used to return silently, which reads exactly like the tool being broken; say why'): returns true iff `rows.some(r => r.length)` (at least one selected layer has at least one animated key anywhere), else shows `SM.t('toastNoKeyOnLayersHint')` and returns false — used only by the Space-edge callback (packet 3), never by the fill-drag (dragLayerBars needs no keys, only a layer selection) nor the top/bottom skew (startLayerSkewDrag, packet 2, operates on ld.inPoint/outPoint, not keys, and has no key guard at all). dragLayerBars (12229-12237): guards on `window.SMLayerInOut && SMLayerInOut.setBarSelection && _layerSel.length`; calls `SMLayerInOut.setBarSelection(_layerSel.map(li => ({li, part:'both'})))` to tag every selected layer as a whole-bar group member; looks up the FIRST selected layer's own `#frame-grid .frow[data-layer="<li>"] .layer-inout-bar` element (returns silently if not found); dispatches a synthetic native `mousedown` MouseEvent at that bar (`bubbles:true, cancelable:true, button:0`, with the CURRENT drag event's `clientX`/`clientY`, no modifier keys set) — handing the entire gesture to layer-inout.js's own bar mousedown listener, which (because `e.target===bar` and no meta/ctrl/shift) calls its own `onDown(li,row,'both',e)`; since the pressed layer is already `_barSel`-selected with length>1 at that instant, onDown takes ITS OWN group-drag branch (layer-inout.js:634+), moving every member's `ld.inPoint`/`ld.outPoint` together AND live-previewing each member's own property-key shift (layer-inout.js:900-919, since dragLayerBars sets no individual key selection so `keySelNow()` reads empty) — owned entirely by layer-inout.js past this call.

packets.signature: startLayerSkewDrag(mode:'top'|'bottom', e:MouseEvent) -> void; onLayerSkewMove(e:MouseEvent) -> boolean (true = event consumed); onLayerSkewUp() -> boolean (true = event consumed)
packets.responsibility: Section header (12239) plus a 4-line design comment (12240-12243: absolute-from-start-of-gesture snapshot, never incremental, same reasoning as startSkewDrag for keys, C20q). `_layerSkew` (12244): the drag's own live state, `null` when no skew is in progress. startLayerSkewDrag(mode,e) (12245-12264), preceded by a 4-line comment on why it re-sorts by visual order (12246-12249): builds `order` = `_layerSel.slice()` sorted by each layer's `.frow[data-layer]` `getBoundingClientRect().top` (same sort as buildLayerRows, independently re-implemented rather than calling it, since it needs `state.layers[li]` per entry, not the flattened key list); calls `pushUndo()` ONCE, unconditionally, before any mutation; sets `_layerSkew = {mode, startX:e.clientX, applied:{}, rows: order.map(li => ({li, origIn:SMLayerInOut.inPointOf(state.layers[li]), origOut:SMLayerInOut.outPointOf(state.layers[li])}))}` — an immutable start-of-gesture snapshot of every row's own current in/out (read through SMLayerInOut's helpers, which fall back to `0`/`state.totalFrames-1` when a layer has no explicit inPoint/outPoint). onLayerSkewMove(e) (12265-12280): returns `false` immediately if no drag is active (the short-circuit contract the sibling-covered onDragMove, motion.js:12934+, relies on: `if (onLayerSkewMove(e)) return;`); computes `total = (e.clientX - _layerSkew.startX) / FC` (signed total dragged distance in frames, using the LIVE global `FC` pixels-per-frame, timeline-zoom.js-owned); for each row `i` of `n = rows.length`, computes `f = n<2 ? 1 : (mode==='top' ? (n-1-i)/(n-1) : i/(n-1))` (linear interpolation by VISUAL RANK, not by frame distance — `mode==='top'`: row 0, the top-most, gets f=1 (moves fully), the bottom-most gets f=0 (anchored); `mode==='bottom'`: the reverse, top-most anchored, bottom-most moves fully), `dx = Math.round(total*f)`, preserves each row's own original duration `w = origOut-origIn`, computes `ni = Math.max(0, origIn+dx)` (floor-clamped to 0, no upper clamp) and WRITES LIVE `ld.inPoint = ni; ld.outPoint = ni+w;` on every tick, records `_layerSkew.applied[li] = ni-origIn` (recomputed fresh from the snapshot every tick, never accumulated) and calls `renderTimeline()` once per tick; returns `true`. Does not touch any property key or stroke content during the drag, and does not call SMEngineBridge.renderNow() itself. onLayerSkewUp() (12281-12294), preceded by a 2-line comment (12283-12284: content and property keys follow ONCE, at drop, same as a bar drag): returns `false` if no drag is active; builds `plan = Object.keys(_layerSkew.applied).map(li => ({li:+li, dx:_layerSkew.applied[li]}))`; clears `_layerSkew = null`; calls `SMLayerInOut.retimeLayers(plan)` ONCE (which, for every nonzero-dx entry, calls `SM.shiftLayerFrames(li,dx)` — sibling-owned, shifts the layer's stored per-frame content — AND `SMMotion.shiftLayerMotionKeys(li,dx)` — sibling-owned, past this span, shifts every animated property's key.frame values — together, per layer); then calls `renderTimeline(); renderLayerList();`, `loadFrame(state.currentFrame)` and `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()`; returns `true`. No second pushUndo call anywhere in this packet — the single checkpoint at the top of startLayerSkewDrag covers the whole move-then-drop gesture as one undo step.
packets.render_path: NO. onLayerSkewMove/onLayerSkewUp mutate `ld.inPoint`/`ld.outPoint`/layer content/keyframes (document data a LATER render reads), and both explicitly ask the engine to repaint (loadFrame/SMEngineBridge.renderNow) as CONSUMERS of the render path, not participants in it — none of the four symbols appears in buildSceneJson/getEffectiveStrokes/export.js (grep-confirmed).

packets.signature: updateLayerStaggerBox() -> void (DOM only, pure geometry read + box create/position)
packets.responsibility: updateLayerStaggerBox (12296-12393): early-returns via removeLayerStaggerBox+return under three guards — not in Motion mode or fewer than 2 selected layers (12297); fewer than 2 of the selected layers actually have a `.frow[data-layer]` row on screen (`spacers`, 12298-12299); `#frame-grid` itself is missing (12300).
